title: Mapping-space criterion for Cartesian edges
statement: Use quasicategories, right-pinched mapping spaces and spaces as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], composition of mapping spaces (postcomposition by an edge) as in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], and inner fibrations and horn-Cartesian edges as in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration between quasicategories in a fixed universe, and let $s:x\to y$ be an edge of $E$. The edge $s$ is $p$-Cartesian in the horn-lifting sense if and only if, for every vertex $z$ of $E$, postcomposition with $s$ and with $p(s)$ gives a homotopy pullback square $$\begin{array}{ccc} \operatorname{Map}_E(z,x)&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_E(z,y)\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ \operatorname{Map}_B(p(z),p(x))&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_B(p(z),p(y)). \end{array}$$ Here a homotopy pullback square of spaces means that the canonical map from its upper left corner to the path-space homotopy fiber product of the other three corners is a weak homotopy equivalence. No existence of other Cartesian lifts is assumed.

source.place: HTT Proposition 2.4.4.3, printed p. 131, stated there in this Cartesian (postcomposition) form; Proposition 2.4.1.8 and Remark 2.4.1.4 identify the Cartesian-edge definition with its horn criterion. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text:
Use the degreewise join and fixed-diagram slices of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. For a diagram $a:K\to C$, write $C_{/a}$ for the simplicial set whose $m$-simplices extend $a$ to $\Delta^m\star K$, and project to $C$ by restriction to $\Delta^m$. In particular $C_{/s}$ uses $K=\Delta^1$ and $C_{/x},C_{/y}$ use $K=\Delta^0$. These projections are right fibrations. Set
$$Q=E_{/y}\times_{B_{/p(y)}}B_{/p(s)},\qquad
\phi:E_{/s}\longrightarrow Q.$$
The first coordinate restricts the final edge $s$ to its target $y$, and the second applies $p$. Both coordinates have the same initial $\Delta^m$ after projection to $B$, so $Q$ projects to $E$ and $\phi$ is over $E$. Put $T_C(a,z)=C_{/a}\times_C\{z\}$, where $z$ denotes the constant simplicial subset. The slice theorem says that each $T_C(a,z)$ is Kan: pull back its right-fibration projection to the Kan complex $\{z\}$ and apply [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber]. For a vertex $v$, $T_C(v,z)=\operatorname{Map}_C(z,v)$ exactly, with the entire initial face constant at $z$.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, construction of the canonical slice map; Corollary 2.1.2.2 and Lemma 2.1.3.3.

proof.text:
The map $\phi$ is a right fibration. A right-horn lifting problem of dimension $m\geq1$, index $0<i\leq m$, transposes, by the degreewise slice definition, to extension over $B$ across
$$(\Lambda_i^m\star\Delta^1)\cup_{\Lambda_i^m\star\{1\}}(\Delta^m\star\{1\})
\hookrightarrow\Delta^m\star\Delta^1.$$
Here the first map $\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ is right anodyne by the definition in [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones], and $\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ is a monomorphism. That node's pushout-join assertion makes the displayed map inner anodyne. An inner fibration lifts such a map: it lifts each generating inner horn by definition, successively extends compatible fillers through pushouts and transfinite compositions (taking their union at a limit), and inherits the lift through a retract. The given inner fibration $p$ therefore supplies the required extension. The transposition keeps the whole prescribed image in $B$, not just its vertices.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, right-fibration assertion; Proposition 2.1.2.1 and Lemma 2.1.2.3, applied directly to slices.

proof.text:
By [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], $\phi$ is trivial Kan precisely when all boundary problems $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq0$, lift. Transposition identifies their domains with
$$(\partial\Delta^m\star\Delta^1)\cup_{\partial\Delta^m\star\{1\}}(\Delta^m\star\{1\})
\hookrightarrow\Delta^m\star\Delta^1=\Delta^{m+2}.$$
Order its vertices as $0,\ldots,m,x,y$. The domain contains the faces omitting $0,\ldots,m$, and the face omitting $x$; it omits exactly the face omitting $y$. Thus it is $\Lambda_{m+2}^{m+2}$, with prescribed final edge $\{m+1,m+2\}=s$. These are exactly all horn problems defining $p$-Cartesian in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], with $n=m+2$. This proves $s$ horn-Cartesian if and only if $\phi$ is trivial Kan. The case $m=0$ is $\Lambda_2^2$, and includes the needed existence of the triangle filler.

source.place: Definition 2.4.1.1, Remark 2.4.1.4, and proof of Proposition 2.4.4.3: explicit boundary/outer-horn correspondence.

proof.text:
For each vertex $z\in E$, restriction over $z$ gives
$$\phi_z:T_E(s,z)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Map}_E(z,y)\times_{\operatorname{Map}_B(p(z),p(y))}
T_B(p(s),p(z)).$$
This is exactly the pullback of $\phi$ to the displayed target, so it is a right fibration: a lifting problem projects to one for $\phi$, and the resulting filler pairs with the prescribed target simplex. The two $T$ spaces are Kan by Step 1. By [lem-coef-infinity-inner-mapping-fiber],
$$\operatorname{Map}_E(z,y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_B(p(z),p(y))$$
is a Kan fibration. Its pullback to $T_B(p(s),p(z))$ is a Kan fibration over a Kan complex, so its total space is Kan (fill the base horn, then lift it). Consequently [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] makes $\phi_z$ a Kan fibration. These statements allow empty mapping spaces and empty fibers.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, restriction to a source vertex; Lemmas 2.4.4.1 and 2.1.3.3.

proof.text: The map $\phi$ is trivial Kan if and only if every $\phi_z$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. If $\phi$ is trivial, each pullback $\phi_z$ lifts all boundaries, and [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion] makes it a weak equivalence. Conversely assume all $\phi_z$ are weak equivalences. They are Kan fibrations by Step 4, so the same criterion says every vertex fiber of each $\phi_z$ is a contractible Kan complex. Every vertex $q\in Q$ projects to a vertex $z\in E$, and the fiber of $\phi$ at $q$ is exactly its fiber as a vertex of the target of $\phi_z$. Thus all vertex fibers of the right fibration $\phi$ are contractible. Apply [lem-coef-right-fibration-contractible-fibers] to conclude that $\phi$ lifts all boundaries, including the empty boundary in dimension zero. This proves both directions without assuming that any other Cartesian lift exists.

For each $z$, consider the strictly commutative square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
T_E(s,z)&\xrightarrow{r_y}&\operatorname{Map}_E(z,y)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
T_B(p(s),p(z))&\xrightarrow{r_{p(y)}}&\operatorname{Map}_B(p(z),p(y)).
\end{array}$$
Here $r_y$ restricts to the final vertex of the specified edge, and the vertical maps apply $p$. Its ordinary pullback comparison is $\phi_z$. Its right vertical map is a Kan fibration by Step 4. The constant-path map from the ordinary pullback to the path homotopy pullback is therefore a weak equivalence by [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison]. The comparison from $T_E(s,z)$ factors as $\phi_z$ followed by that map. Two-out-of-three for the induced maps on components and homotopy groups shows that this strict square is a homotopy pullback if and only if $\phi_z$ is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, final paragraph: the strict pullback computes the homotopy pullback.

proof.text:
Restriction to the source vertex $x$ of $s$ gives
$$r_x:T_E(s,z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_E(z,x).$$
This is a trivial Kan fibration, for the following explicit reason. A boundary lifting problem in degree $m\geq0$ is extension from
$$(\partial\Delta^m\star\Delta^1)\cup_{\partial\Delta^m\star\{0\}}(\Delta^m\star\{0\})
\hookrightarrow\Delta^m\star\Delta^1.$$
The domain contains every face except the one omitting $x$, so it is the inner horn $\Lambda_{m+1}^{m+2}$. The edge $s$ is already in that domain, and so is the whole initial face $\Delta^m$, fixed constant at $z$. A quasicategory filler therefore retains both restrictions. Apply the identical argument in $B$ to obtain $r_{p(x)}:T_B(p(s),p(z))\to\operatorname{Map}_B(p(z),p(x))$. Both maps are homotopy equivalences by [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence], and they commute strictly with $p$. In particular $m=0$ uses the inner horn $\Lambda_1^2$, not a Cartesian lifting assumption.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.4.4.3, interpretation of the source corner; the special case of the dual of Proposition 2.1.2.5 is proved by its single inner-horn calculation.

proof.text:
Identify the composition and its coherence in the strict presentation. For $C=E$ or $B$, let $a:u\to v$ be respectively $s$ or $p(s)$, and let $w$ be $z$ or $p(z)$. Given $t\in T_C(a,w)_m$, precompose $t:\Delta^{m+2}\to C$ with the monotone map
$$[m]\times[2]\longrightarrow[m+2],\quad
(i,0)\mapsto i,\quad(i,1)\mapsto m+1,\quad(i,2)\mapsto m+2.$$
This gives a simplex of $V(w,u,v)$ in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Its edges $01,12,02$ are respectively $j r_u(t)$, the constant edge $a$, and $j r_v(t)$, where $j$ is the natural right-pinch inclusion of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. These formulas respect all simplicial operators. By the defining composition equation in the composition node, the roof
$$\operatorname{Map}_C(w,u)\xleftarrow{r_u}T_C(a,w)\xrightarrow{r_v}\operatorname{Map}_C(w,v)$$
therefore represents postcomposition by $a$. The prism also supplies its triangle witness, rather than only an equation of homotopy classes. Applying $p$ to the prism gives exactly the prism for $B$, including every higher simplex. Thus the two roofs with their vertical maps specify the coherent postcomposition square.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, its explicit strict interpretation of the composition square; the right-pinch and triangle formulas are checked against the existing composition construction.

proof.text: Use the strict roof of Steps 6-8 as the representative of the coherent square in the statement: the two left corners are presented by $T_E(s,z)$ and $T_B(p(s),p(z))$, with the natural homotopy equivalences $r_x,r_{p(x)}$ to the stated left corners. Its horizontal arrows and commutation data are the postcomposition arrows and witnesses of Step 8. This is precisely the slice representative prescribed in HTT, rather than a square supplied with an independently chosen commutation homotopy. To check the same presentation in the arrow-space model, postcompose the horizontal maps and both right corners with the natural pinch maps $j$. This is a strictly commuting map of squares, identity at the two left corners and a homotopy equivalence at the two right corners. Its three-corner cospans meet the exact equations of [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance], so their path homotopy pullbacks are weakly equivalent and their fourth-corner comparisons commute. Thus this change of model preserves the homotopy-pullback test. Inverting the equivalences in the two left roofs specifies the canonical coherent composition square, whose homotopy-pullback test is computed by this strict representative. The prism construction ensures that this is the coherence stipulated by composition, not merely arrows that agree on components.

split_report.summary: Proved the Cartesian mapping criterion by the fixed-edge join slice, its boundary/outer-horn identification, the vertex-fiber test for a right fibration, and a path-pullback comparison. Wrote the prism giving postcomposition and its functorial coherence; used existing nodes only. No statement change and no project attachment found. HTT read online but not archived; proof_origin is agent.

Steps 1 and 4 take from its statement that a right fibration over a Kan complex lifts all horns and has Kan total space; it is a generic simplicial-set black box of unit sk-prop-sf-cbc, and no node of sk-prop-sf-biduality-general states it (same-unit siblings already use it as a tool).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N4-af1067a23 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The proof is correct and complete. I read the item, all 10 steps, the full statements of the 14 cited nodes, the unit route, the blueprint ancestor and the citer lem-coef-arrow-target-cartesian-pullbacks. HTT is not archived under literature/, so I checked the steps against HTT Prop. 2.4.4.3 from my knowledge of the text; the worker records it as WANTED. The statement is unchanged and has exactly HTT's hypotheses (inner fibration, quasicategories, one edge). Its commutation datum is made precise as the slice roof (Steps 8-9), which is canonical because the homotopies between two sections of the trivial fibration r_{p(x)} form a contractible space. Step 2: the pushout-join clause applies with A=Λ^m_i and {1}⊂Δ^1. Step 3: the boundary domain is exactly Λ^{m+2}_{m+2} with final edge s, and m=0 is Λ^2_2. Step 4: φ_z is a Kan fibration, via lem-coef-infinity-inner-mapping-fiber and lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber. Step 5: both directions are right, and contractible-fibers needs no condition on the base. Step 6: the strict comparison is φ_z and the right leg is a Kan fibration. Step 7: the boundary domain is the inner horn Λ^{m+2}_{m+1}. Step 8: the prism edges are j r_u, the constant edge and j r_v, giving postcomposition = [r_v][r_u]^{-1}. Small cases agree: N([1]) over a point, p=id, B=pt. No new nodes, no cycle, no duplicate (the cocartesian criterion is the opposite orientation). Not a target node, so no base-change morphism or coefficient category is involved; no SGA source. lean.statement: theorem infinity_cartesian_mapping_criterion (E B : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory E] [Quasicategory B] (p : E ⟶ B) (_hp : InnerFibration p) (x y : E _⦋0⦌) (s : Δ[1] ⟶ E) (_hsx : E.δ 1 (SSet.yonedaEquiv s) = x) (_hsy : E.δ 0 (SSet.yonedaEquiv s) = y) : IsCartesianEdge p s ↔ ∀ z : E _⦋0⦌, ∃ (u : (arrowMappingSpace E x y) _⦋0⦌) (g : cartesianPostcompositionSource E z x y u ⟶ cartesianPostcompositionSource B (p.app _ z) (p.app _ x) (p.app _ y) ((arrowSpaceMap p x y).app _ u)), (arrowMappingSpaceInclusion E x y).app _ u = diagramVertex s ∧ g ≫ cartesianPostcompositionInclusion B (p.app _ z) (p.app _ x) (p.app _ y) ((arrowSpaceMap p x y).app _ u) = cartesianPostcompositionInclusion E z x y u ≫ (ihom Δ[2]).map p ∧ IsHomotopyPullbackSquare (cartesianPostcomposition E z x y u) g (arrowSpaceMap p z y) (cartesianPostcomposition B (p.app _ z) (p.app _ x) (p.app _ y) ((arrowSpaceMap p x y).app _ u))
lean.note: Reviewer fix: presents the canonical coherent postcomposition square by its fixed-second-edge triangle roofs (the slice representative of node Steps 8-9), built by base change of the recorded spineRestriction, as in the landed cocartesian dual lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion. The point u and the left vertical map g are fixed by monomorphic ambient inclusions; the right vertical map is the existing arrowSpaceMap. Natural right-pinch equivalences identify these models with the right-pinched mapping spaces of the node. The delivered version used canonicalPostcompositionMap for E and B, each an independent Classical.choose of a composition representative known only up to homotopy, so IsHomotopyPullbackSquare (which needs strict commutation) could fail for an edge that is Cartesian, e.g. for an automorphism p.
